newsitem.title: USA: Amoco says to sell some U.S. properties.
newsitem.headline: Amoco says to sell some U.S. properties.

text.p: Amoco Corp said it will sell a number of U.S. oil and natural gas properties and royalty interests as part of a major refocusing of its U.S. exploration and production business.

The assets being considered are about one-third of Amoco's U.S. working interest properties and represented about 15 percent of total U.S. reserves and 10 percent of U.S. net production in 1996, said the energy giant.

"This divestment will allow us to redeploy future capital and resources from non-core areas to core producing areas, while improving the profitability and reducing the complexity and costs of our U.S. operations," said Richard Flury, executive vice president responsible for Amoco's exploration and production business.

"The long-term success of our U.S. upstream business demands this type of aggressive portfolio management," he said. "By focusing our limited human and capital resources on a smaller, financially superior asset base, our U.S. upstream business will remain a significant contributor."
The properties will be grouped in as many as five separate packages. They are located in Wyoming, Colorado, New Mexico, Oklahoma and on the Gulf Coast, Amoco said.
In addition to reserves, the packages may include operating centers, selected processing plants and gathering systems and other infrastructure, the company said.

"These packages will be very attractive to regional players that can capture greater synergies and efficiencies," Flury said. "One or more of these packages might also provide sufficient critical mass for a new entrant to establish an anchor position in a new geographical area."

Amoco said it would not comment on anticipated proceeds or on the amount of overhead costs that would be reduced as a result of the divestment. Cash generated would be used to fund growth opportunities in and outside North America, it said.
The company said it hired Morgan Stanley as financial advisor. It plans to start marketing the properties early in the third quarter and hopes to complete the sales by year-end.
"The company has not yet determined the impact the divestment will have on employees. Amoco will continue to keep them informed as the process moves forward," it said.
